question: Should OpenClaw accept the experimental grouped-update mutation contract before live package-installer and Gateway partial-state recovery are demonstrated and documented?
rationale: The unresolved question is not a narrow coding defect: it determines whether `update_partial` reporting alone is an acceptable operator experience for shared plugin, configuration, and scheduler mutations.

options.title: Require live recovery proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until redacted live package, Gateway cron, and retained-artifact recovery evidence demonstrates the operator path after an uncertain external mutation.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Reduce the apply stage to owners with demonstrably recoverable local mutations and defer package or cron mutation until their recovery interfaces are ready.

options.title: Accept partial-state reporting
options.body: Land the stated experimental contract with `update_partial` as the recovery signal, accepting that operators may need manual intervention for retained external state.

recommendation.title: Require live recovery proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until redacted live package, Gateway cron, and retained-artifact recovery evidence demonstrates the operator path after an uncertain external mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: His review names the unresolved lifecycle and operator-recovery decision directly.
